privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: The privacy notice covers all of Animal and Plant Health Agency’s work.
privacy.moreInformation: More detailed information on how we manage personal data for each of our functions is included within
privacy.dataCollectedByHeading: Your data is being collected by
privacy.dataController: The data controller is the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) for personal data that you give to the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).
privacy.aphaDataProtectionManager: APHA is an Executive Agency of Defra. You can contact APHA’s Data Protection Manager by email at:
privacy.jointControllers: APHA also works with the Scottish Government and Welsh Government, who are joint controllers with APHA for any relevant personal data.
privacy.dataQuestions: Any questions about how Defra and APHA are using your personal data and your associated rights should be sent to the above contact.
privacy.dataProtectionOfficer: The Data Protection Officer responsible for monitoring that Defra and APHA is meeting the requirements of the legislation can be contacted by email at:
privacy.dataCollectedIntro: The personal data collected is made clear in
privacy.dataCollectedSuffix: or documentation that collects personal data.
privacy.dataObtainedHeading: How your data has been obtained
privacy.dataObtainedIntro: We have obtained your data either directly from you or a third party. How your data has been obtained in any particular case is made clear in
privacy.dataObtainedSuffix: or documentation that collects personal data.
privacy.whyDataHeading: Why APHA is using your data
privacy.whyDataIntro: Personal data is collected and stored to support APHA’s functions which include:

functions.function-1: identifying and controlling endemic and exotic diseases and pests in animals, plants and bees, and surveillance of new and emerging pests and diseases
functions.function-3: facilitating international trade in animals, products of animal origin, and plants
functions.function-4: protecting endangered wildlife through licensing and registration
functions.function-5: safeguard animal health and welfare; and protect human health where relevant (zoonoses)
functions.function-6: managing a programme of bee inspections, diagnostics, research and development, and training and advice
functions.function-7: regulating the safe disposal of animal by-products to reduce the risk of potentially dangerous substances entering the food chain
functions.function-8: employee data necessary to support staff management
functions.function-9: the safeguarding of employees, sub-contractors and customers (this may include very limited use of body worn video when necessary)
functions.function-10: for APHA’s statutory functions in relation to plant biosecurity; the environmental release of genetically modified organisms; and in the management of alien and invasive species - specifically for notifiable pests and diseases, imports and export controls, training and for statutory food safety monitoring purposes

privacy.moreAboutApha: More information about APHA can be found at
privacy.googleAnalyticsIntro: Our website uses Google Analytics, a web analytics service provided by Google, to monitor site activity and gather insights into how users interact with our content.
privacy.googleAnalyticsData: This data allows us to understand user behaviour better and implement improvements to enhance your experience on our site. As part of this process, Google Analytics collects certain information, including your IP address. This data helps us determine approximate locations, enabling us to identify potential areas for user research and better tailor our services to meet users’ needs.
privacy.googleAnalyticsPurpose: Please note that the information collected is used solely for analytical and improvement purposes.
privacy.googleAnalyticsPrivacy: We respect your privacy and are committed to handling your data responsibly. For more information on how Google collects and processes data, please refer to
privacy.legalBasisHeading: The legal basis for processing your data

legalBases.legalBase-1: the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller
legalBases.legalBase-2: for compliance to a legal obligation on the controller
legalBases.legalBase-3: the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering a contract
legalBases.legalBase-4: you have given us consent to process your data for one or more specified purposes

privacy.consent: Where the legal basis for processing your personal data is your consent, you can opt out at any time and details of how you can do that are made available to you by the team that is processing your personal data.
privacy.requirementHeading: A legal or contractual requirement to provide personal data
privacy.requirement: Sometimes you are legally or contractually required to share personal data by APHA. These situations are made clear in the relevant privacy notices.
privacy.consequencesHeading: Consequences of not providing the necessary data

consequences.consequence-1: For statutory and public interest purposes it is necessary to provide data as stated in the relevant legislation.
consequences.consequence-2: For contractual based processing, your entrance into a contract with us is voluntary and necessary information is supplied to fulfil that contractual relationship.
consequences.consequence-3: For consent based processing you have a right to revoke this at any given time.

privacy.automatedDecisionHeading: Personal data used for automated decision making
privacy.automatedDecision: The information you provide is not connected with individual decision making, in other words making a decision solely by automated means without any human involvement.
privacy.profilingHeading: Personal data fused or automated 'profiling' and the consequences of this
privacy.profiling: The information you provide is not connected with profiling, in other words automated processing of personal data to evaluate certain things about an individual.
privacy.sharingHeading: Who APHA shares your data with

sharing.sharing-1: Personal data may be made available to local authorities and other public bodies in the UK and EU to meet legal requirements and regulatory and enforcement functions.
sharing.sharing-2: We may share data with Defra and its agencies, Welsh Government, Scottish Government, Northern Ireland Executive, Food Standards Agency and other official organisations and enforcement authorities.
sharing.sharing-3: We may share data with other organisations working for us to enable us to carry out our duties.
sharing.sharing-4: We may have to release information (including personal data and commercial information) under the following legislation:

legislation.legislation-1: UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR)

privacy.confidentiality: We will not allow any unwarranted breach of confidentiality and we will not act in contravention of our obligations under UK data protection legislation.
privacy.outsideUkHeading: Storing and using personal data outside the UK

outsideUk.outsideUk-1: A very small percentage of government records containing personal information are selected for permanent preservation at the National Archives. They are made available in accordance with the Freedom of Information Act 2000, as amended by the Data Protection Act 2018.
outsideUk.outsideUk-2: The data you provide will largely not be transferred outside of the UK. On rare occasions, when it is lawful and complementary to our work carried out in the public interest, research data may be transferred securely outside of the UK.

home.intro: Use this service to apply for a TB movement licence. You must have a licence before moving cattle onto or off a farm or premises with TB restrictions.
home.checkExistingLicence: Check if APHA has already sent you a TB movement licence before you apply.
home.youCanUseThisService: You can use this service to apply for a licence if you are moving cattle:

movingCattleReasons.reason-1: from an unrestricted farm or market to a TB restricted farm or premises
movingCattleReasons.reason-2: from a TB restricted farm or premises to:

reason-2-options.option-1: a TB restricted farm or premises
reason-2-options.option-2: an approved finishing unit (AFU), including enhanced with grazing (AFUE)
reason-2-options.option-3: slaughter or a TB slaughter gathering (red market), unless covered by a general licence

movingCattleReasons.reason-3: from an AFU (including AFUE) to an AFU (including AFUE)

home.whenYouDoNotNeedThisService: When you do not need this service
home.generalLicenceNotice: You don’t need to apply if a general licence already allows the movement.
home.generalLicenceCheck: Check the general licence APHA sent you when your herd was placed under TB restriction. A general licence will allow you to move cattle:

home.movingBetweenRestrictedPremises: Moving cattle between TB restricted farms or premises
home.movingBetweenRestrictedPremisesIntro: If cattle are moving from a TB restricted farm or premises to another TB restricted farm or premises, the destination farm or premises must apply for the licence. This is because we need details about their TB biosecurity procedures.

home.intro: Use this service to apply for a movement licence during a foot and mouth disease outbreak.
home.youCanApplyForFollowing: You can use this service to apply for a licence for the following activities:

activities.activity-1: movement of live animals on or off your premises

home.aphaNeedDetails: APHA need these details to process your application:
home.signingIntoServiceIntro: You need a Defra account to use this service. You can register for one using your Government Gateway sign in details.
home.signingIntoServiceDetails: After you sign in you need to enter your contact information, and details about your business if you have one.
home.getHelpText: If you need help using the service you can call 03000 200 301. Lines are open from Monday to Friday between 8.30am and 5pm.
home.privacyNoticeIntro: How we use your personal data is set out in the
home.privacyNoticeLinkText: exotic, notifiable and reportable diseases privacy notice (opens in a new tab)

submit.additionalInfo: Licences can take up to 5 days to issue. For welfare cases, we will aim to process applications sooner.
